abstract: Biofilm formation is ubiquitous in the marine environment, driven by microbial colonization on submerged surfaces, and poses ongoing challenges to maritime industries. In this study, whole-genome sequencing (WGS) was carried out for Acinetobacter junii IK2, a strain isolated from the biofilm formed on stainless steel coupons immersed in a seawater microcosm setup to elucidate its genomic features and biofilm-forming potential. The genome consists of 3,215,808 bp with a GC content of 38.63%, assembled from Illumina-generated sequencing data. A total of 2990 protein-coding sequences (CDS), 10 rRNA genes, and 63 tRNA genes were predicted. Functional annotation through COG, GO, and KEGG databases resulted in the classification of 2909, 2389, and 2960 unigenes, respectively. Genome analysis identified the presence of thirteen genes associated with biofilm development, including the pgaABC operon, two-component systems (barA, ompR), and global regulators (crp, csrA, dksA), suggesting potential for biofilm formation. Genes such as oxyR, yfiB, yiaD, and pal further support oxidative stress resistance, adhesion, and envelope stability. The biofilm-forming ability of Acinetobacter junii IK2 was further validated using a crystal violet microtiter plate assay, confirming its ability to form biofilms. Additionally, 35 virulence genes, 6 multidrug resistance genes and 25 insertion sequences suggest enhanced survival, pathogenicity and genetic plasticity, reinforcing biofilm-mediated persistence. These genomic features provide insights into potential adaptive mechanisms that may contribute to the environmental adaptation of A. junii IK2 and offer insights into its role in the marine environment.
